title: Russell indulged him, in and out of the band like a spoiled child
summary: Russell was easygoing and let Holmes come and go as he pleased, which Holmes now sees as taking advantage of him.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Because I was not... I was not an easy person to get along with. You know what I mean? And Russell was the nicest person you ever wanted to meet in your life. He'd just sit and smile at everything. He would grin. He was agreeable to anything. And me, I was just arrogant enough to take advantage of it. He liked me. He liked me very much. He liked the work I was doing, you know. But I was really taking advantage of him. Not for money. Money never...

I was never money-crazy. You know, some people are just greedy after money. But no, I liked to have a good time, I liked to enjoy myself. And music, that was my life! That's the only reason I played music, because I liked the life. It made things go so nice and easy. Beautiful. Everything was a good time. People are happy. And I liked music, because I was happy most of the time. If there was something going on at the Savoy Ballroom and we were working across the street at the Saratoga Club, well, I knew that's where the attraction was, at the Savoy, and I was going to be over there, too. I would be over there. My horn would
be in the Saratoga Club, but I'd be over at the Savoy. And I come back and I tell Russell about it, what's going on over there, this-that-and-the-other -- he'd just smile.

He never said nothin' to me about anything. I just did as I pleased. And he liked it. I could quit the band any time I wanted. If he'd go out on some one-nighters or something, and I didn't feel like it... In other words, I was kind of like a spoiled child. I didn't realize -- you know what I mean -- what things meant to me. I didn't realize the value of them.
